steps.question: Which shape roles does it need?
What should control corners say?
steps.why: Rounded by default; each brand sets its own corner.
Each brand sets its own corner through the theme.

steps.pick: radius.4: We use the 4px control corner for Aster's growing boxes in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving a list item or a text area the curve of the controls beside it. So fields and rows read as one family, because Aster's control corner is small, not a pill (shape.values).

steps.question: Which color roles does it need?
steps.why: Each brand brings its own accent ramp.

steps.question: How saturated is the palette?
steps.why: Balanced, so any brand hue works.

steps.rule: A recessed fill, a step below content.
steps.pick: neutral.100, a step below content (1.1:1 on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.
steps.darkPick: neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the page's canvas, for table headers and wells in dark, in order to show depth by tone, 1.16:1 under content and 1.03:1 under the canvas. The darker fill does this by the depth rule turned downward: what sits lower is darker. So a well reads as recessed and never as a raised card, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

steps.why: Motion is reduced, not removed: a fade keeps the change visible, and nothing slides.
